title: PHP interrupted session shutdown can retain a freed filename pointer
summary: A fatal error during session cleanup can preserve a script-filename pointer after request memory is freed. Later requests in the same worker can trigger use-after-free and a crash.

severity.rationale: The demonstrated impact is memory corruption and worker crashes after specialized failing session cleanup. Code execution through this specific field has not been demonstrated.

exposure: The application must allow cleanup to fail in the documented manner, and subsequent requests must reuse the same worker. Authentication requirements depend on that application path.

params.instructions: Check PHP session extension version, affected release line and the documented exposure conditions.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 on the corresponding line.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed release meets the corresponding fixed version and verify the affected workflow with harmless test inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
